notes: Baseline is near-ceiling on raw detection: Fable 5 with the project constitution in context scored 23/25 without the skill. The skill's measured delta is precision and form, not raw catch-rate.

Both baseline failures are house-idiom precision items: it flagged the planted decoy RetryCfg's 'Cfg' abbreviation (idiomatic under §9 and rex-code-ergonomics), and it never stated the from/to swap-compatibility risk on transfer() despite four other findings on that function.

The skill's largest effect is report form: 48 vs 393 lines (eval-0), 39 vs 258 (eval-1), 76 vs 183 (eval-2) for equal-or-better coverage, with all three with-skill reports in the identical table format, BLOCK/REFACTOR/NIT severity, and Clean/Not-checked disclosure sections. Reports are mergeable across audits; baselines each invented their own structure.

Non-discriminating evals: eval-1 (7/7 both configs) and eval-2 (4/4 both configs) did not separate the configs. The planted API-naming defects are too easy for this model; if iterating, harden eval-1 with subtler violations or accept it as a regression floor.

Eval-2 side effect worth acting on: both configs independently converged on the same real production defects in src/adapters/ (unbounded Retry-After reaching a sleep on the order path; both-sides-empty snapshot never emits is_last_chunk and wedges the Polymarket hot book after a BookReset; rest_quiet's 'shared' doc header describes sharing that does not exist; backoff jitter does not decorrelate concurrent actors). Independent convergence is strong evidence these are genuine.
Time/token columns are zero because the subagent idle notifications carried no usage data; the 5-8x report-length ratio is the only cost proxy available.
Run-harness flake: 3 of 6 subagents went idle before saving report.md and needed one nudge message each; report contents were unaffected.
